title: Combining Conditions with Logical Operators
objectives: Use && to require all conditions to be true.
Use || to require at least one condition to be true.
theory: Logical operators combine Boolean expressions. The AND operator && returns true only if both operands are true. The OR operator || returns true if at least one operand is true. The NOT operator ! inverts a Boolean.
if (age >= 13 && age < 18) is true only if both conditions are true. This checks a range. if (hasWeapon || hasShield) is true if the player has either item or both. This offers alternatives.
Complex conditions become unreadable without parentheses. if (score >= 50 && bonus > 0 || lives > 0) is ambiguous. Rewrite as if ((score >= 50 && bonus > 0) || lives > 0) for clarity.
De Morgan's Law states !(a && b) is equivalent to !a || !b and !(a || b) is equivalent to !a && !b. These are useful for simplifying negations.
Combining conditions is powerful but can become confusing. A rule of thumb: keep single if conditions to three comparisons. More complex logic belongs in a helper method.
